source_kinds.measured: Derived from data. Requires n, derived_from, date, reference_frame.
source_kinds.invariant: An implementation or anatomical contract, not a measurement. Requires rationale.
source_kinds.external: Taken from a published table, rig asset or spec. Requires derived_from or cites.
source_kinds.provisional: Explicitly unvalidated. Requires rationale. The value may be wrong.

notes.frame: typical_deg and max_deg are ANATOMICAL angles. The rest-relative bound is anatomical + the bone's rest offset, DERIVED at load time by rigby_poc.analysis.anatomy.neutral.rest_offset. It is deliberately not stored here: it is geometry rather than an authored value, and several offsets sit within 1e-5 deg of a rounding boundary, which made this file architecture-dependent. See plan 04 6.4.
notes.mirroring: flexion and abduction are preserved across sides; only twist negates. Authored once, applied to both.
notes.enforceable: 'mutation_only' marks a bone compiler.py never assigns a rotation to on any path, so its limit can never fire from generated motion. Exercising it belongs to plan 06.
notes.enforcement: 04b shipped every check report-only. 04c gates on `enforced`, set by rigby_poc.analysis.anatomy.authored_rom.is_enforced: the bound must be cited (external or invariant), the bone must be reachable from generation, and the bone must not be the root. Everything else stays report-only and reports its measurement.
notes.thumb_range_widened: Thumb typical ranges were widened to their max on 2026-08-28. The table already records that the thumb is the one chain where the authored asset and the anatomical frame disagree, that the rig crate_grip preset closes the thumb by adduction rather than flexion, and that these limits are the least trustworthy in the table. A conservative range on an axis that is already the wrong axis buys nothing and costs the reach a grasp needs.

Worse, the rig's own crate_grip preset drives all three thumb segments about an axis that decomposes to pure abduction with a zero flexion component -- so a thumb flexion limit would constrain a DOF the rig's authored grip never uses. It is not established that flexion is the right DOF to limit here at all. Bounds are wide rest-relative sanity checks.
source.reference_frame: none -- no anatomical neutral exists for this entity

angular_rate_limits.$comment: Peak angular speed per joint class, deg/s. The envelope until now bounded only where a joint may be, never how fast it may get there, so a compiled clip could move a bone its whole range inside one frame and nothing in the manifests objected. Measured consequence: the hand crossed from preshape to contact fast enough to strike the block and send it 7 cm across the table before any finger had closed. A position envelope cannot express that, because every pose along the way was legal.
angular_rate_limits.units: degrees per second, applied to the anatomical DOF angle

source.rationale: Voluntary reaching speeds, not ballistic maxima. Humans can drive most of these joints far faster -- a thrown punch or a snapped finger is several times these numbers -- but a reach toward an object a hand is about to grasp is deliberate, and that is the motion being bounded. Values are placed proximal-slow to distal-fast, which is the ordering limb inertia imposes.

near_contact_rate_limits.$comment: MEASURED AND NOT APPLIED. Peak angular speed per joint class while the hand is within near_contact_distance_m of the object, deg/s. Written to stop a thumb at 0.49 m/s throwing a 0.25 kg block to 1.99 m/s, which it would; but applying it destroys the grasp, because the digits then cannot close in the time available -- the lift falls from 19.99 cm to 1.31 at these values and is still gone at 160 deg/s, while the block's peak speed is 0.46 m/s either way. The flick was a symptom of digits welded rigidly to commanded poses; compliant welds and closure that stops at contact address the cause. Kept because the numbers are real and a future controller may want them.
near_contact_rate_limits.units: degrees per second, applied to the anatomical DOF angle
